pr_title: [DisplayServer] Add method to check if native window is focused.
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/77824

In some cases `Window` object callbacks are set after it's shown, and focus event arrived, therefore it's necessary to check current window status.

issue_context.title: Initial window focus state is incorrect, `has_focus()` returns `false` when it should return `true`
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.3.stable.official [5222a99f5]

### System information

Windows 11, AMD Ryzen 5 3500U with Radeon Vega Mobile Gfx     2.10 GHz

### Issue description

  The "focus" of a window through get_window ().has_focus () reports false for a window initially even though it is obviously true.  It doesn't get corrected until something else gets the "focus" and it receives a WM_SETFOCUS again.  This is the case for the Editor window when running a plug-in aswell.

  It looks like the internal "focus" state flag is being reset after the initial WM_SETFOCUS has occurred for a window.

### Steps to reproduce

  Run the MRP and you'll see that "false" is printed in the title-bar of the window when it should be "true".

### Minimal reproduction project

[MRP_Focus.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/11644644/MRP_Focus.zip)
comments:
It cannot be reproduced on Linux Mint 21.1 (Cinnamon 5.6.8/i3wm) if you just press F5/F6 to run.

After running, before the window is displayed normally (during the black screen), if other programs get the focus (clicked on other applications including editor), it will first output `false`. This does not seem to be a bug.
If the window has the focus and input is directed to the window and it is reporting that it doesn't have the focus, then that is a bug.
This seems to be a Windows platform specific issue, I was able to reproduce the issue on Win10. Running with F5/F6 also shows no focus.

review_comments: "had" focus? Looks like a typo but I'm not sure.
Not it's saving the state to restore it later. If it _had_ focus, it will be restored.
It's a state saved before removing native windows, which is checked after deletion.
